prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests where the Accept header lists only application/json (server previously required both application/json AND text/event-stream to be present), causing valid JSON-only clients to get a 406 Not Acceptable. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects requests where the Accept header lists only application/json (server previously required both application/json AND text/event-stream to be present), causing valid JSON-only clients to get a 406 Not Acceptable. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts. #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that splits the Accept header into media-range entries, strips q-params, and excludes entries with q=0, then matches type/subtype including wildcards (e.g. */*, application/*). #2046 instead replaces the check with a plain acceptHeader?.includes('application/json') substring test, which does not exclude explicitly-disabled entries like application/json;q=0 (it still contains the substring 'application/json' and would incorrectly pass) and does not recognize wildcard Accept values -- cases #1996's parser handles correctly.

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same Accept-header validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts. #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that splits the Accept header into media-range entries, strips q-params, and excludes entries with q=0, then matches type/subtype including wildcards (e.g. */*, application/*). #2046 instead replaces the check with a plain acceptHeader?.includes('application/json') substring test, which does not exclude explicitly-disabled entries like application/json;q=0 (it still contains the substring 'application/json' and would incorrectly pass) and does not recognize wildcard Accept values -- cases #1996's parser handles correctly.

members.title: chore(client): normalize trailing slashes in discovery paths
members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both fix buildWellKnownPath/buildDiscoveryUrls only stripping a single trailing slash from the pathname (via `endsWith('/') → slice(0,-1)`), which leaves malformed double-slash discovery paths like `/foo//.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` when the input path has multiple trailing slashes. Both replace the single-strip logic with a `.replace(/\/+$/, '')` regex on the same lines of buildWellKnownPath and buildDiscoveryUrls.
